title: [Spike] Quantify inter-runner variance before matrixing the Locust sweeps
summary: Matrixing BM-15's four pool-size sweeps would put the compared configurations on different runner VMs, injecting hardware variance into the exact axis being measured. Measure that variance before deciding what can safely be split.
description:
`locust-scale` runs eight load steps strictly serially: BM-14a (5 m) + BM-14b (5 m) + BM-14c (3 m) + BM-15 pool=1/5/10/20 (2 m each) + oversaturation (1 m) = 22 minutes of pure load time on one runner, plus per-step ramp-up, on top of one Db2 boot. `benchmark-nightly` runs a similar serial block.

A `strategy: matrix` is the obvious fix, and for BM-14a/b/c it is straightforwardly safe — they are independent scenarios, reported separately, never compared to each other.

BM-15 is different. Its four pool sizes are a *comparison*: the whole point is how latency and error rate move as `DB2_POOL_SIZE` goes 1 → 5 → 10 → 20. That comparison is only meaningful if all four ran on comparable hardware. GitHub-hosted runners vary between VMs — different physical hosts, different noisy neighbours — so a matrix would inject inter-runner variance directly into the measured axis. The variance could plausibly exceed the effect being measured, which would make the benchmark actively misleading rather than merely noisier.

Work:

- Run the identical BM-15 pool=5 configuration on 5+ separate runner VMs and compute the spread in p50/p95 latency and throughput.
- Compare that spread against the *effect size* between pool=1 and pool=20 on a single runner.
- If inter-runner spread is small relative to the pool-size effect, matrixing BM-15 is safe. If it's comparable or larger, BM-15's sweeps must stay co-located and only BM-14 gets split.
- Separately confirm the Db2 boot cost after CIW-3 (and CIW-9 if it landed): each matrix leg pays a full boot, so at a 12-minute boot a 4-way split of an 8-minute block is a net loss. Establish the break-even.
- Note that splitting *does* improve isolation between scenarios — BM-14b's 100-agent sweep currently shares a runner and a Db2 instance with the pool-saturation tests. Whether that's contaminating current results is worth checking while the harness is instrumented.

Deliverable: a comment recording the variance numbers and the go/no-go decision for CIW-13.

comments.author: implementation
comments.text: Spike preparation complete. Variance measurement workflow created at .github/workflows/runner-variance-check.yml. To run: Actions → 'Runner variance check (CIW-12)' → Run workflow with repetitions=5. Run once with pool_size=5 to measure spread; run again with pool_size=1 and pool_size=20 on a single runner to get the effect size baseline. Decision rule: if spread (max-min/median) < 20% of the pool=1 vs pool=20 effect size → matrixing BM-15 is safe → proceed to CIW-13 with full scope. If spread >= 20% → keep BM-15 co-located, only matrix BM-14a/b/c → proceed to CIW-13 with reduced scope. Note: run this measurement AFTER CIW-3 (healthcheck tightened) to get representative boot times for the break-even calculation.
